transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Yeah… I mean, I’m probably making it sound bigger than it is, but I’ve just been having a rough time since I moved into this busted-up room. Stuff keeps going wrong there—leaks, heat problems—so I’m up late trying to fix things, and then I’m dragging the next day.

I’ve been snapping at people more than I should, which I don’t like. And I’ve been late to work, messing up things I normally handle fine. I figured maybe I should come in before it gets worse, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed yourself feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even when it’s not about the problems with your room?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I’m, like, depressed or anything. I still like the same stuff, I think. It’s more like when I’m stressed about the room, it kind of follows me around, if that makes sense. But outside of that, I haven’t really noticed losing interest in things.
Have you been feeling unusually worried, restless, or on edge lately, even when you’re not thinking about the problems with your room?

Um… not really, I don’t think. I mean, I get worked up when something’s going on with the room, sure, but if I’m not thinking about that stuff, I wouldn’t say I’m just on edge for no reason. At least, I haven’t noticed it like that. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you ever had sudden episodes where you felt intense fear or discomfort that came out of nowhere, like your heart was racing, you couldn’t breathe, or you felt like something terrible was going to happen?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been stressed, yeah, but I haven’t had anything where it just hits out of nowhere like that, like I can’t breathe or something terrible’s happening. At least not that I can remember.
Have you noticed any days where you feel down, empty, or hopeless, even when things with the room are going okay?
Not really… I mean, I have off days like anybody, I guess, but I wouldn’t say empty or hopeless. If the room stuff is calm, I’m usually okay. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, you know?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, even when there isn’t a clear problem, or do your worries feel more specific to the issues in your room?

It’s more specific to the room, I think. Like, I don’t sit around worrying about everything for no reason. It’s just since I moved into that busted-up place, it’s been… a lot. I end up staying up dealing with leaks or the heat, and then I’m tired and late to work, and I’ve snapped at people more than I should. I’m not trying to make excuses, but that’s really what it seems tied to.
Looking back over the past few months, have you ever felt anxious or down even when things in your life other than the room seemed to be going okay?

Yeah… I guess when I really look at it, it’s mostly tied to that room. I came in because ever since I moved into that busted-up place, I’ve been snapping at people more, staying up trying to deal with leaks or the heat, and then I’m dragging myself into work late and messing up stuff I normally handle fine.

I don’t want to make it sound like my whole life is falling apart or anything… but it’s been getting to me.
Have you noticed any symptoms like trouble sleeping, low energy, or difficulty concentrating that happen even when you're not dealing with problems in your room?

Not really when the room isn’t acting up, I don’t think. It’s more like… when I’m up dealing with the leak or the heat and then I don’t sleep right, so I’m dragging the next day and I’m late to work or I mess up stuff I usually handle fine.

I don’t want to overstate it, but yeah, that’s when it happens. It feels tied to that busted-up room more than just coming out of nowhere.
Can you think of any time in the past month when things in your life, aside from your room, were going fine, and yet you still felt down, anxious, or had trouble functioning?

Honestly, I can’t really think of a time like that. I mean, maybe I’ve had normal off days, but the stuff that made me come in has really been tied to that room.

Ever since I moved into that busted-up place, I’ve been snapping at people more than I should, staying up trying to deal with leaks or the heat, and then I’m dragging myself into work late and messing up things I usually handle fine. So… if everything else was okay and the room wasn’t a problem, I don’t think I was still falling apart or anything. Does that make sense?
